name: Criminology and Criminal Justice, BS (Boston)
disclaimer: NU Map is an independent, student-built planner. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or officially connected to Northeastern University. Data is scraped from Northeastern's public catalog and refreshed on a schedule; always confirm with the official catalog and an academic advisor.

legend.notes: Sentences quoted verbatim from the catalog page that state a condition we could NOT express as structure — exclusions ("Research courses may not be used"), eligibility lists, per-course grade minimums. A section can consist of nothing but these. Quote them; never infer from them that a particular course does or does not satisfy the section.
legend.creditsRequired: Semester hours the catalog states for a section whose courses it does not list. Do not add these into a program total: some restate credit that another section already counts.

requirementSections.title: Introduction to Crime, Law, and the Justice System
notes: What do we know about crime and justice? In these three courses successful students will develop a foundational understanding of three related phenomena: why crime exists, how our criminal justice system responds to crime, and the constitutional and legal oversight of this process.

requirementSections.title: Current Crime and Justice Issues
notes: These courses introduce students to topical issues related to crime and justice.

requirementSections.title: Understanding and Experiencing Criminal Justice Institutions and Systems
notes: How does justice work and for whom? These courses introduce students to the systems and institutions tasked with providing justice. Each includes experiential learning components in cooperation with local criminal justice institutions.

requirementSections.title: Preparing for Co-op
notes: The following course is designed to prepare students to apply for and embark on their first co-op. Students who do not take a co-op may replace EESH 2000, CRIM 3000, and CRIM 4000 with an additional CRIM elective.

requirementSections.title: Creating Knowledge About Crime and Justice
notes: How do we know what we know about crime and justice—and how do we develop new knowledge? Harnessing data to learn about issues, identify solutions, and advocate for change.

requirementSections.title: Crime Problems
notes: The following courses offer students a deeper look at a range of crime problems.

requirementSections.title: Systemic Issues
notes: A consideration of systemic issues facing the criminal justice system.

requirementSections.title: Returning from Co-op
notes: Allows students the opportunity to reflect on their co-op experience and its connection to their ongoing coursework and future plans:

requirementSections.title: Solutions and Reform
notes: How do we reinvent criminal justice institutions and their practice? The capstone experience is project based and solution oriented, drawing on knowledge gained in the classroom and through co-op and other experiences.

requirementSections.title: Returning from Co-op (2)
notes: Allows students the opportunity to reflect on their co-op experience and its connection to their ongoing coursework and future plans:

requirementSections.title: Criminal Justice Electives
notes: Rounding out knowledge of crime and justice.
Complete five additional CRIM electives. Four must be from the 3000, 4000, or 5000-level.
